title: Why every developer needs a portfolio site

slides.heading: Your GitHub is not a portfolio
slides.body: Recruiters spend seconds on a profile. Raw repos don't tell them what you can actually build.

slides.heading: It controls the first impression
slides.body: A profile shows your code. A portfolio shows your judgement — what you chose to build, and why.
bullets: You pick the framing, not the algorithm
You decide what gets seen first
You explain the why behind the what

slides.heading: It is proof you ship
slides.subtitle: Deployed beats described
slides.body: A live URL settles the question a CV only raises. Anyone can claim React. A working app proves it.
bullets: One deployed project outweighs five tutorials
Uptime is a skill nobody lists but everyone notices
Bugs you fixed in public read as experience

slides.heading: It compounds while you sleep
slides.body: Applications end when you stop sending them. A site keeps working — search, referrals, old links.
bullets: Easy for someone to forward on your behalf
One link answers every version of "what do you do?"

slides.heading: Ship one page this week
slides.body: Not a redesign. One page: who you are, three things you built, how to reach you. Improve it later.
